categories.name: Mitigation
categories.tagline: Assets and activities that cut emissions today
categories.description: The original Climate Bonds Taxonomy pillar: a science-based map of the physical assets, technologies and projects needed to decarbonise the global economy in line with a 1.5-2°C pathway. Used by issuers and investors to screen green, sustainability-linked and transition instruments.

categories.name: Resilience
categories.tagline: Investments that strengthen preparedness for climate risk
categories.description: Launched alongside the Climate Bonds Standard v4.3, the Resilience Taxonomy is the first globally applicable, science-based framework for identifying investments that make a substantial contribution to climate adaptation and resilience, spanning infrastructure, water, agriculture, nature and cities.

categories.name: Blue
categories.tagline: Financing a sustainable, climate-resilient ocean economy
categories.description: The Blue pathway extends Climate Bonds criteria into marine and coastal systems: ports, shipping, fisheries, aquaculture and blue-carbon ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrass and salt marsh, connecting ocean-economy finance to the wider Mitigation and Resilience taxonomies.

categories.name: Methane Abatement
categories.tagline: Fast, high-impact cuts to a super-pollutant
categories.description: Methane has more than 80 times the warming power of CO2 over 20 years. Climate Bonds' methane work spans oil & gas fugitive emissions, waste and landfill gas, and agrifood, mobilising debt finance behind measurement, verification and abatement technologies that deliver near-term climate impact.

sectors.name: Energy Generation, Grids & Storage
sectors.description: Solar, wind, geothermal, marine renewables, bioenergy, and the grids and storage that carry them.
sectors.overview: Energy is the founding sector of the Climate Bonds Taxonomy. Criteria cover generation technologies with near-zero direct emissions, plus the transmission, distribution and storage assets needed to integrate them, using technology-specific and, where relevant, emissions-intensity thresholds.
eligibleActivities: Solar PV and solar thermal generation
Bioenergy meeting feedstock and lifecycle-emissions tests
Electrical grid upgrades enabling renewables integration
Battery and other energy-storage assets dedicated to low-carbon generation
technicalCriteria: Direct life-cycle emissions intensity thresholds by technology
Dedication tests for shared transmission infrastructure
sectors.certificationNotes: Solar, Wind, Geothermal and Marine Renewable Energy criteria are available for certification under the Climate Bonds Standard; Bioenergy and Grids & Storage criteria are used alongside sector-specific eligibility tests.

sectors.name: Low Carbon Buildings
sectors.description: Residential, commercial and mixed-use buildings meeting top-tier local energy performance.
sectors.overview: The Buildings Criteria certify new and existing residential and commercial buildings using a mix of absolute energy-performance thresholds, best-in-class local market benchmarks, and pathway-based trajectories aligned with 1.5°C decarbonisation of the built environment, updated in December 2023 and aligned with the EU Taxonomy's Substantial Contribution criteria for climate mitigation.
eligibleActivities: New-build residential and commercial construction meeting top 15% local performance
Building components: efficient HVAC, envelope, on-site renewables
technicalCriteria: Embodied carbon considerations for new build
sectors.certificationNotes: Buildings Criteria are fully available for certification and are one of the most widely used sector criteria in the Certified Bonds Database.

officialLinks.label: Climate Bonds & the EU Taxonomy on Buildings

sectors.name: Low Carbon Transport
sectors.description: Passenger and freight rail, mass transit, electric vehicles and water-borne transport.
sectors.overview: Transport criteria cover the vehicles, rolling stock, vessels and supporting infrastructure that deliver the deepest emissions cuts per passenger- or tonne-kilometre, prioritising electrified rail and mass transit while setting emissions ceilings for other modes including shipping.
eligibleActivities: Bus rapid transit and zero-emission bus fleets
Water-borne passenger and freight transport meeting emissions thresholds
technicalCriteria: gCO2/passenger-km or tonne-km thresholds by mode
Alignment with Shipping Criteria for water-borne assets
sectors.certificationNotes: Low Carbon Transport Criteria are available for certification; the flagship case study is the Société du Grand Paris 'Grand Paris Express' rail programme.

sectors.name: Industry & Heavy Materials
sectors.description: Steel and other hard-to-abate heavy industry decarbonisation pathways.
sectors.overview: Industry criteria target hard-to-abate materials production, starting with Steel, using emissions-intensity benchmarks per tonne of output that tighten over time, recognising both best-available-technology retrofits and near-zero pathways such as green hydrogen-based direct reduced iron.
eligibleActivities: Electric arc furnace steelmaking with high scrap/DRI content
Carbon capture retrofits on heavy industry
technicalCriteria: tCO2e per tonne of crude steel thresholds (Steel Criteria, Feb 2024)
Pathway alignment with sectoral decarbonisation trajectories
sectors.certificationNotes: Steel Criteria are available for certification; further heavy-industry sub-sectors (cement, chemicals) are in development.

sectors.name: Waste Management
sectors.description: Landfill gas capture, recycling infrastructure and waste-to-value systems.
sectors.overview: Waste Management criteria cover collection, sorting, recycling and treatment infrastructure that diverts material from landfill and captures residual methane, explicitly excluding high-emissions incineration-without-capture and prioritising circular-economy outcomes.
eligibleActivities: Landfill gas capture and utilisation on closed sites
technicalCriteria: Methane capture-efficiency thresholds for landfill gas
sectors.certificationNotes: Waste Management Criteria are available for certification and are directly cross-referenced by the Methane Abatement taxonomy work.

officialLinks.label: From Waste Policy to Targeted Methane Abatement

sectors.name: Information & Communication Technology
sectors.description: Data centres, networks and digital infrastructure powered by low-carbon electricity.
sectors.overview: ICT criteria address the fast-growing emissions footprint of data centres and telecom networks, combining energy-efficiency metrics (PUE), renewable-power procurement, and hardware lifecycle considerations so digital infrastructure investment can be screened alongside physical assets.
eligibleActivities: Energy-efficient telecom towers and edge infrastructure
Submarine and terrestrial fibre supporting grid digitalisation
sectors.certificationNotes: ICT criteria are in development as part of the broader taxonomy update program; interim screening uses Taxonomy Table guidance.

sectors.name: Agriculture
sectors.description: Low-carbon cropland, livestock and agrifood systems.
sectors.overview: Mitigation-side Agriculture criteria are under active development, targeting practices that cut on-farm and supply-chain emissions: precision fertiliser use, low-emissions livestock management, and agrifood methane abatement, closely coordinated with the Forestry & Land Use and Methane Abatement workstreams.
eligibleActivities: Low-emissions livestock feed and manure management
technicalCriteria: Exclusion criteria for deforestation-linked supply chains
sectors.certificationNotes: Full Agriculture Criteria are in development; interim guidance draws on the Taxonomy Tables and Methane Abatement roadmap.

officialLinks.label: A Roadmap to Catalyze Methane Abatement (PDF)

sectors.name: Forestry & Land Use
sectors.description: Afforestation, sustainable forest management and land-use carbon sinks.
sectors.overview: Forestry & Land Use criteria identify activities that protect and expand natural carbon sinks: certified sustainable forestry, afforestation and reforestation with native or mixed species, and avoided-deforestation financing, with explicit safeguards against land-use conflicts and biodiversity loss.
eligibleActivities: Afforestation and reforestation with native/mixed species
Avoided deforestation and forest conservation finance
sectors.certificationNotes: Forestry criteria are available for certification, often paired with Blue-Carbon (mangrove) criteria for coastal projects.

sectors.name: Water Infrastructure
sectors.description: Efficient, low-carbon water supply, reuse and catchment infrastructure.
sectors.overview: Water Infrastructure Criteria evaluate assets from industrial water efficiency and reuse to catchment restoration and large-scale supply infrastructure, covering hybrid 'green-grey' and nature-based solutions alongside conventional treatment and distribution systems.
eligibleActivities: Water treatment and distribution efficiency upgrades
Nature-based and hybrid green-grey water infrastructure
technicalCriteria: Energy-intensity per unit of water treated/moved
sectors.certificationNotes: Water Infrastructure Criteria are available for certification; the Vadodara Municipal Corporation green bond is a certified real-world example.

sectors.name: Marine Renewable Energy
sectors.description: Tidal, wave and other ocean-based renewable power generation.
sectors.overview: Marine Renewable Energy criteria certify tidal-stream, wave and other ocean-energy generation assets, plus the dedicated transmission infrastructure connecting them to shore, using near-zero emissions-intensity thresholds consistent with the wider Energy sector.
eligibleActivities: Dedicated subsea transmission for marine renewables
technicalCriteria: Emissions-intensity threshold consistent with Energy sector
Dedication test for shared transmission assets
sectors.certificationNotes: Marine Renewable Energy Criteria are available for certification; EnBW's EUR 500m certified issuance is a recent real-world example.

sectors.name: Hydrogen Production
sectors.description: Renewable-powered electrolytic hydrogen and low-carbon derivatives.
sectors.overview: Hydrogen Production criteria set a life-cycle emissions-intensity threshold for hydrogen and derivatives (ammonia, e-fuels), designed to be technology-neutral so electrolysis powered by additional renewable generation and other low-carbon production routes can both qualify if they meet the same bar.
eligibleActivities: Electrolytic hydrogen using additional renewable power
Low-carbon derivatives: green ammonia, e-methanol, e-fuels
Dedicated hydrogen transport and storage infrastructure
technicalCriteria: Additionality requirement for renewable electricity input
sectors.certificationNotes: Hydrogen Production Criteria are available for certification, developed via extensive technical working group consultation.

sectors.name: Carbon Capture & Storage
sectors.description: Point-source capture, transport and geological storage of CO2.
sectors.overview: Carbon Capture and Storage criteria (in development) evaluate capture retrofits on hard-to-abate industry, dedicated CO2 transport pipelines, and permanent geological storage, with strict permanence and monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) requirements to guard against leakage.
eligibleActivities: Point-source capture on heavy industry and hydrogen production
sectors.certificationNotes: CCS criteria are in development as part of the industrial-decarbonisation taxonomy work.

sectors.name: Low Carbon Manufacturing
sectors.description: Electrification and efficiency upgrades across manufacturing processes.
sectors.overview: Low Carbon Manufacturing criteria (in development) extend the Industry pathway beyond heavy materials to broader manufacturing processes, covering electrification of thermal processes, waste-heat recovery, and equipment upgrades that measurably cut process emissions.
sectors.certificationNotes: Criteria are in development; Steel Criteria can be used today for eligible steel-manufacturing activities.

sectors.name: Climate Adaptation Pathways
sectors.description: Cross-cutting framework for evaluating substantial contribution to resilience.
sectors.overview: The Climate Bonds Resilience Taxonomy (CBRT) sets out seven resilience themes and a common evaluation process: demonstrate climate-risk exposure, show a measurable resilience benefit, and screen out maladaptation, so any sector — from energy to agriculture — can assess an investment's adaptation value.
eligibleActivities: Climate-risk and vulnerability assessment for an asset or system
Resilience-benefit measurement against a defined baseline
Integration with existing Mitigation Sector Criteria
technicalCriteria: Alignment with Climate Bonds Standard v4.3 governance
sectors.certificationNotes: Resilience Certification launched with Climate Bonds Standard v4.3 following 2025 public consultation.

sectors.name: Nature-Based Solutions
sectors.description: Ecosystem restoration that buffers climate risk for people and infrastructure.
sectors.overview: Nature-Based Solutions within the Resilience Taxonomy recognise wetlands, mangroves, floodplains and urban green infrastructure as resilience assets in their own right — reducing flood and heat risk while delivering co-benefits for biodiversity and carbon storage.
eligibleActivities: Wetland and floodplain restoration for flood attenuation
Urban green/blue infrastructure for heat and flood resilience
sectors.certificationNotes: Assessed under the Resilience Taxonomy; closely linked to Blue-Carbon and Forestry criteria for coastal and forest ecosystems.

sectors.name: Water Resilience
sectors.description: Water systems hardened against drought, flood and supply disruption.
sectors.overview: Within the Resilience Taxonomy's Water theme, eligible investments demonstrably reduce vulnerability to drought, flood or water-quality shocks — from diversified supply and demand-management to flood-resilient treatment works — evaluated alongside the Mitigation-side Water Infrastructure Criteria.
eligibleActivities: Flood-proofing of treatment and pumping infrastructure
Demand management and leakage reduction under stress scenarios
technicalCriteria: Alignment with Water Infrastructure Sector Criteria where relevant
sectors.certificationNotes: Certifiable under Resilience Certification when paired with underlying Water Infrastructure eligibility.

sectors.name: Resilient Infrastructure
sectors.description: Energy, transport, ICT and water infrastructure hardened for a changing climate.
sectors.overview: The Resilient Infrastructure theme organises investments into energy, transport, ICT and water infrastructure sub-sectors, each assessed for measurable reductions in climate-risk exposure — such as grid hardening against extreme heat or transport assets protected from flooding.
eligibleActivities: Climate-resilient ICT/data infrastructure siting and design
Redundancy and backup systems for critical infrastructure
sectors.certificationNotes: One of four sub-sectors explicitly named in the Climate Bonds Resilience Taxonomy methodology.

sectors.name: Agricultural Resilience
sectors.description: Farming systems adapted to shifting rainfall, heat and pest pressure.
sectors.overview: Agricultural Resilience covers investment in climate-adapted crop varieties, irrigation efficiency under water stress, and diversified farming systems that reduce yield volatility from climate shocks, evaluated distinctly from (but often paired with) mitigation-focused Agriculture criteria.
sectors.certificationNotes: Assessed under the Resilience Taxonomy; frequently cross-referenced with Nature-Based Solutions.

sectors.name: Urban & Coastal Cities Resilience
sectors.description: Urban systems addressing heat, flood and sea-level risk.
sectors.overview: Cities-focused resilience investment addresses urban heat-island effects, pluvial/fluvial flood risk and, for coastal cities, sea-level rise — spanning drainage upgrades, cooling infrastructure and building-level adaptation, evaluated alongside the Buildings mitigation criteria.
technicalCriteria: Co-benefit alignment with Buildings mitigation criteria
sectors.certificationNotes: Assessed under the Resilience Taxonomy's Cities theme; complements Coastal Protection in the Blue taxonomy for coastal cities.

sectors.name: Ocean Economy
sectors.description: The umbrella framework connecting marine sectors to Climate Bonds criteria.
sectors.overview: Ocean Economy is the connective sector for Blue finance, linking marine renewable energy, ports, shipping, fisheries and blue-carbon ecosystems into a single investable narrative for sovereign, corporate and municipal blue-bond issuers.
technicalCriteria: Cross-reference to Marine Renewable Energy, Shipping, Fisheries & Aquaculture and Blue Carbon criteria
sectors.certificationNotes: Ocean Economy financing typically certifies via the specific underlying sector (Marine Renewable Energy, Shipping, etc.).

sectors.name: Marine Infrastructure & Ports
sectors.description: Low-carbon, climate-resilient port and marine infrastructure.
sectors.overview: Ports and marine infrastructure criteria address shore-power electrification, low-carbon cargo-handling equipment, and climate-resilient design against sea-level rise and storm surge, connecting Blue-sector infrastructure to both Mitigation and Resilience taxonomies.
eligibleActivities: Climate-resilient port design against sea-level rise/storm surge
sectors.certificationNotes: Uses Shipping Criteria for vessel-facing assets and Resilient Infrastructure criteria for coastal-protection elements.

sectors.name: Shipping
sectors.description: Vessels and fuels for low-carbon maritime transport.
sectors.overview: Shipping Criteria evaluate vessels and propulsion systems against emissions-intensity thresholds, covering newbuild low/zero-emission vessels, retrofits (wind-assist, air lubrication), and alternative marine fuels, aligning with IMO decarbonisation trajectories.
eligibleActivities: Retrofit efficiency technologies (wind-assist, air lubrication, hull coatings)
Alternative marine fuels meeting life-cycle thresholds
sectors.certificationNotes: Shipping Criteria background work is published; full certification pathway sits within the Transport/Blue overlap.

sectors.name: Fisheries & Aquaculture
sectors.description: Sustainable seafood production within ecological limits.
sectors.overview: Fisheries & Aquaculture eligibility centres on sustainable-yield fishing practices, low-impact aquaculture siting and feed sourcing, and traceability systems, aiming to protect marine biodiversity while supporting coastal livelihoods and food security.
technicalCriteria: Siting restrictions to protect sensitive habitats
sectors.certificationNotes: Criteria are in development; current guidance draws on the wider Taxonomy Tables and marine biodiversity safeguards.

sectors.name: Coastal Protection
sectors.description: Hard, hybrid and nature-based defences against sea-level rise and storm surge.
sectors.overview: Coastal Protection spans engineered sea defences, hybrid green-grey structures and nature-based buffers, assessed for measurable risk reduction to coastal communities and infrastructure, bridging the Blue and Resilience taxonomies.
eligibleActivities: Sea walls, levees and storm-surge barriers
Managed retreat and relocation support infrastructure
technicalCriteria: Preference ordering favouring nature-based options where feasible
sectors.certificationNotes: Assessed jointly under Blue and Resilience (Cities, Nature-Based Solutions) taxonomies depending on project design.

sectors.name: Blue Carbon: Mangroves, Seagrass & Salt Marsh
sectors.description: Coastal-wetland ecosystems that store carbon and buffer storms.
sectors.overview: Blue Carbon criteria recognise mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes as dual mitigation-and-resilience assets: protecting and restoring them locks in carbon while providing storm-surge and erosion buffering for adjacent communities.
sectors.certificationNotes: Evaluated jointly under Forestry & Land Use (carbon) and Nature-Based Solutions / Coastal Protection (resilience) criteria.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas Methane Abatement
sectors.description: Fugitive-emissions detection, capture and elimination across the value chain.
sectors.overview: The oil & gas methane workstream mobilises debt finance behind leak detection and repair (LDAR), routine-flaring elimination, and equipment upgrades that cut fugitive and vented methane across upstream, midstream and downstream operations — a 'Fast Track to Net Zero' priority given methane's near-term warming impact.
eligibleActivities: Methane-capture-and-use at wellheads and processing facilities
sectors.certificationNotes: Financed via Sustainability-Linked or transition instruments referencing the Methane Abatement roadmap; dedicated certification criteria are in development.

officialLinks.label: A Roadmap to Catalyze Methane Abatement in Oil & Gas (PDF)

sectors.name: Waste & Landfill Methane
sectors.description: Capturing methane from municipal solid waste and closed landfill sites.
sectors.overview: Methane from decomposing organic waste is one of the most tractable abatement opportunities: landfill-gas-capture retrofits, diversion of organics from landfill, and wastewater-treatment methane capture all deliver rapid, measurable reductions and are directly cross-referenced with the Waste Management sector criteria.
eligibleActivities: Landfill gas capture and flaring/utilisation retrofits
sectors.certificationNotes: Uses Waste Management Sector Criteria for certification, with methane-specific MRV overlays.

officialLinks.label: From Waste Policy to Targeted Methane Abatement

sectors.name: Agrifood Methane Abatement
sectors.description: Enteric fermentation, manure management and rice-cultivation methane.
sectors.overview: Agrifood methane sources — livestock enteric fermentation, manure management and flooded rice cultivation — are large but historically under-financed; Climate Bonds' work in this area coordinates with national and sector taxonomies to define bankable abatement interventions.
technicalCriteria: Verified methane-intensity reduction per unit of output
sectors.certificationNotes: Full certification criteria are in development; guidance draws on the wider Methane Abatement roadmap and Agriculture sector work.

officialLinks.label: From Ambition to Alignment: Integrating Methane into Tomorrow's Taxonomies

sectors.name: Coal Mine & Mining Methane
sectors.description: Capturing methane released from active and abandoned coal mines.
sectors.overview: Coal-mine methane (from ventilation air and drainage systems) and abandoned-mine methane are potent, concentrated emissions sources; abatement investment covers drainage-and-capture systems, ventilation air methane oxidation, and mine-closure methane management.
technicalCriteria: Verified capture volumes vs. baseline venting
Exclusion of new thermal-coal capacity expansion
sectors.certificationNotes: Certification criteria are in development; interim financing typically structured as sustainability-linked instruments with methane KPIs.

caseStudies.title: Grand Paris Express
caseStudies.bondSize: Multi-tranche, part of Europe's largest infrastructure programme
caseStudies.impact: 200km of new metro and commuter rail lines and 68 new stations, certified under Low Carbon Transport Criteria.
caseStudies.lessons: Large, multi-decade infrastructure programmes can be certified in phases as construction and financing tranches progress.

caseStudies.title: NAB SDG Green Bond Programme
caseStudies.impact: Refinances loans across Solar, Wind, Low Carbon Transport, Marine Renewable Energy and Low Carbon Buildings criteria.
caseStudies.lessons: Programmatic certification lets banks certify a lending portfolio once and issue repeatedly against the same certified framework.

caseStudies.title: Vadodara Municipal Corporation Green Bond
caseStudies.impact: Financed water-sector improvements for the city of Vadodara under Water Infrastructure Criteria.
caseStudies.lessons: Municipal green bonds are a viable route for mid-sized cities to finance certified water infrastructure.

caseStudies.title: EnBW Marine Renewable Energy Bond
caseStudies.impact: Financed marine renewable energy projects certified under Marine Renewable Energy Criteria.
caseStudies.lessons: Utilities can use certified bonds to signal credibility for less mainstream renewable technologies like tidal and wave.

caseStudies.title: Huadian New Energy Group Solar & Wind Bond
caseStudies.impact: Financed solar and wind generation projects certified under Solar and Wind Sector Criteria.
caseStudies.lessons: Large state-owned generators use Certification to access lower-cost capital for renewable build-out at scale.

faqs.question: Is solar power eligible under the Climate Bonds Taxonomy?
faqs.answer: Yes. Onshore solar PV and solar-thermal generation, plus dedicated transmission infrastructure, are eligible under the Energy sector's Solar Criteria, which are available for certification under the Climate Bonds Standard.

faqs.question: What does the Low Carbon Transport Criteria cover?
faqs.answer: Electrified rail, mass transit, zero-emission road vehicles, cycling infrastructure and water-borne transport meeting mode-specific emissions-intensity thresholds. Shipping has its own dedicated background criteria.

faqs.question: What documents are required to get Climate Bonds Certified?
faqs.answer: Issuers typically need: a pre-issuance Verifier's Report confirming alignment with the relevant Sector Criteria, disclosure of use-of-proceeds and management-of-proceeds processes per the Climate Bonds Standard, and post-issuance annual reporting including an updated Verifier's Report.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Mitigation and Resilience taxonomies?
faqs.answer: Mitigation criteria certify assets that directly cut greenhouse-gas emissions (e.g. a wind farm). Resilience criteria, launched with Standard v4.3, certify investments that make a substantial, measurable contribution to withstanding and adapting to climate hazards (e.g. flood-resilient water infrastructure), while screening out maladaptation.

faqs.question: How does Agriculture differ between Mitigation and Resilience?
faqs.answer: Mitigation-side Agriculture criteria (in development) focus on cutting on-farm and supply-chain emissions. Resilience-side Agricultural Resilience focuses on adapting farming systems to climate hazards like drought and heat, reducing yield volatility. A single farm investment can potentially qualify under both if it both cuts emissions and improves resilience.

faqs.question: Why does Climate Bonds treat methane abatement separately?
faqs.answer: Methane has more than 80 times the 20-year warming potential of CO2, so abatement delivers outsized near-term climate benefit per dollar invested. Climate Bonds mobilises finance behind measurement, verification and abatement technology across oil & gas, waste and agrifood specifically because these interventions are fast, high-impact and currently under-financed.

faqs.question: How do I certify a bond under the Climate Bonds Standard?
faqs.answer: Select eligible assets against the relevant Sector Criteria, engage an Approved Verifier for a pre-issuance review, disclose use-of-proceeds and management processes, obtain Certification before or at issuance, then report annually with an updated Verifier's Report to maintain Certification.

faqs.question: Is the Blue taxonomy separate from Mitigation?
faqs.answer: Blue is best understood as a lens applied across sectors: Marine Renewable Energy sits under Mitigation, while Shipping, Ports, Fisheries and Blue Carbon draw on both Mitigation and Resilience criteria depending on the specific investment.

glossary.definition: A science-based classification of the assets, activities and projects needed to deliver a Paris-aligned, low-carbon and climate-resilient economy.
The ICMA-aligned governance framework (currently v4.3) that Sector Criteria sit under, covering use-of-proceeds, verification and reporting requirements.
A formal Climate Bonds label confirming a debt instrument, asset or entity meets the Climate Bonds Standard and applicable Sector Criteria.
Technical, science-based eligibility thresholds developed per sector (e.g. Solar, Buildings, Water) that define what counts as eligible for Certification.
An independent, Climate Bonds-approved assurance provider who confirms a bond or issuer meets the relevant criteria before and after issuance.
The requirement that at least 95% of net proceeds from a Certified instrument fund eligible green/resilient assets and projects.
Debt instruments whose financial terms are linked to the issuer achieving predefined sustainability performance targets, rather than tied to specific projects.
The Climate Bonds framework identifying investments that make a substantial contribution to climate adaptation and resilience, launched with Standard v4.3.
A green or sustainability bond whose proceeds fund ocean-economy, marine or coastal projects such as sustainable fisheries or blue-carbon restoration.
Interventions that measurably reduce methane emissions from oil & gas, waste, agriculture or mining sources.
The systems used to quantify an intervention's emissions or resilience impact, report it transparently, and have it independently verified.
A route allowing an issuer to certify a lending or asset framework once and apply it across repeated bond or loan issuances.
Annual disclosure, including an updated Verifier's Report, required to maintain Certification after a bond is issued.
Consistent with the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting global warming to well below 2°C, pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.
An International Platform on Sustainable Finance initiative mapping common ground between major taxonomies (e.g. EU and China) to reduce fragmentation.

certificationPathway.name: Idea
certificationPathway.description: Identify a financing need tied to climate-aligned assets or projects.

certificationPathway.name: Project & Asset Selection
certificationPathway.description: Select the specific projects or assets that will back the instrument.

certificationPathway.name: Eligibility Screening
certificationPathway.description: Check candidate assets against the relevant Sector Criteria eligibility tests.
requirements: Confirm category: Mitigation, Resilience, Blue or Methane

certificationPathway.name: Criteria Application
certificationPathway.description: Apply the detailed technical thresholds (emissions intensity, resilience benefit, etc.) to each asset.

certificationPathway.name: Verification
certificationPathway.description: Engage an Approved Verifier to conduct a pre-issuance assurance review.
requirements: Provide evidence for each eligibility test

certificationPathway.name: Certification
certificationPathway.description: Submit the Verifier's Report and supporting disclosures for formal Climate Bonds Certification.

certificationPathway.name: Issuance
certificationPathway.description: Issue the Certified bond or loan, referencing the Climate Bonds Certification mark.

certificationPathway.name: Reporting
certificationPathway.description: Publish annual allocation and management-of-proceeds reporting.

certificationPathway.name: Impact Reporting
certificationPathway.description: Report the environmental/resilience impact delivered, verified by an updated Verifier's Report.
requirements: Impact metrics disclosure (e.g. tCO2e avoided, resilience benefit)
